settings.persistent.title: Persistent mode
settings.persistent.description: Starts OpenPulsar with the session, directly in the system tray, and keeps keyboard commands active.
settings.persistent.restart.title: Persistent mode
settings.persistent.restart.enabled.body:
Persistent mode will be enabled the next time OpenPulsar starts.

OpenPulsar will start automatically with your Linux session and remain active in the system tray.

OpenPulsar must be restarted to apply this change.
settings.persistent.restart.disabled.bod:
Persistent mode will be disabled the next time OpenPulsar starts.

OpenPulsar will no longer start automatically with your Linux session and will behave like a regular application.

OpenPulsar must be restarted to apply this change.
settings.led_correction.title: LED color correction
settings.led_correction.description: Adjusts the intensity of the Red, Green and Blue channels sent to your mouse LEDs. Changes are applied immediately and do not affect the colors displayed in OpenPulsar.
help.polling.title: Polling Rate
help.polling.body:
How often the mouse sends its position to the PC.

125 Hz = 8 ms
250 Hz = 4 ms
500 Hz = 2 ms
1000 Hz = 1 ms

For gaming, 1000 Hz is generally recommended.
help.debounce.title: Debounce
help.debounce.body:
Filtering time for mechanical contacts.

A lower value slightly reduces latency but may increase the risk of unintended double-clicks.
help.lod.title: Lift-Off Distance (LOD)
help.lod.body:
Height at which the sensor stops tracking movement when the mouse is lifted.

Available values depend on the detected model, for example 0.7 mm, 1 mm or 2 mm.
help.motion_sync.title: Motion Sync
help.motion_sync.body:
Synchronizes sensor data with USB reports.

It can improve motion consistency at the cost of a very small latency increase.
help.angle_snap.title: Angle Snap
help.angle_snap.body:
Automatically corrects movement to favor straight lines.

Recommended:
✗ FPS
✓ Drawing
✓ Office use
help.ripple_control.title: Ripple Control
help.ripple_control.body:
Filters some of the sensor noise.

It can improve tracking stability but slightly reduces responsiveness.
help.dpi.title: DPI (Dots Per Inch)
help.dpi.body:
Determines how far the cursor moves for the same physical mouse movement.

Low value:

✓ More precision
✗ More hand movement

High value:

✓ Faster movement
✗ Less precision
help.led_correction.title: RGB gain
help.led_correction.body:
Adjusts the Red, Green and Blue channels sent to the LEDs.

Changes are applied immediately and do not affect the colors displayed in OpenPulsar.
help.left_click_lock.title: Locked button
help.left_click_lock.body:
This button is currently assigned to Left Click.

At least one button must always keep this action.

Assign Left Click to another button first to modify this one.

about.title: About OpenPulsar
about.body:
Free configurator for Pulsar mice on Linux.

NEED

Pulsar mice work on Linux, but their official configuration software is not available there. Some settings therefore remain difficult to access.

OpenPulsar addresses this need with a native, open-source application for configuring your mouse easily on Linux.

PHILOSOPHY

Configuring a mouse should be simple, fast and understandable.

OpenPulsar favors a clear interface, user control and genuinely useful features. The hardware you buy belongs to you; its settings should remain accessible and under your control.

THANKS

OpenPulsar builds on the work of the community that documented and analyzed Pulsar peripheral communication protocols.

GET INVOLVED

OpenPulsar grows through feedback and contributions from its community. You can help by testing new models, reporting bugs, improving translations or contributing code.

Join the project on GitHub or Discord.
